Subject: BrightCart launch: request for quota bump & traffic forecast

Team —

BrightCart confirmed their public beta->GA launch window: target date Nov 18. They asked us to confirm that we can support a short-term traffic surge during the cross-region rollout. I attached the customer forecast (launch_traffic_model_v2.csv) and the filled quota_request_form.pdf. High-level asks from Sales/Customer: 

- Temporary increase to per-customer rate limits (burst allowance) for 48 hours around GA
- A soft upper bound on concurrent requests and a fallback model routing plan if we throttle
- SRE & Product sign-off on monitoring and rollback triggers

Customer-provided numbers (from BrightCart): ~10M tokens/day average first week, with spikes up to 800 rps sustained for 10–15 minutes per region during promo pushes. They expect auth traffic to arrive from US-EAST and US-WEST primarily. Marissa, can you confirm the source of these numbers (sheet attached)? Karthik & Laura — can you review feasibility and list what we need from the customer (headers, exact model sizes, prediction of token length distribution) to size the temporary quota bump?

Requested timeline:
- Need internal sign-off on quota/rate policy by EOD Nov 12
- Final mutual action plan (MAP) with BrightCart by Nov 14

If we can't support the full spike without affecting other tenants, propose alternatives (canary percentage, shorter burst windows, or routing to smaller quantized model).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: BrightCart launch: request for quota bump & traffic forecast

Vanessa — thanks for the heads up. Quick clarifying Qs before we size the request: 

- Which model(s) will BrightCart use at peak (name + parameterization / quantization)?
- Expected average prompt+completion token length (we need a distribution, not just averages)
- Are they using streaming or non-streaming generation endpoints?

Rough notes from infra POV: a sustained 800 rps spike for 10–15 minutes at GA in two regions could saturate the shared pools unless we either: (a) route BrightCart to a dedicated reserved pool for the GA window, or (b) accept a very short-term global burst allowance with strict rollback triggers. Dedicated pool gives isolation cost to the account (we can price that into the MAP).

Operational asks if we proceed with a temporary global burst: 
- Canary rollout plan (we recommend staged ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% over 3 hours, with automatic rollback on latency or error thresholds)
- Concrete SLO thresholds for errors (5xx) and 95th percentile latency for insert points
- SRE runbook stub (who will own pager, escalation)

I attached SLO exemption notes (slo_exemption_notes.docx) with initial rollback thresholds. If the customer is using a smaller quantized variant for high-volume paths we could accept higher rps for the same cost.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer, Head of Infra — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Thanks — I pulled the attached traffic model and ran a quick simulation. Preliminary product ask/constraints: 

- We can support the request if we have a documented canary: 25% traffic for the first 6 hours in one region, followed by expansion if all KPIs (error rate, token latency, cost delta) are within thresholds.
- Need the customer to agree to an automatic downgrade to a smaller quantized model if tail latency or error rate hits the threshold. We should pre-configure model-routing rules in the MAP to avoid manual toggles.
- If BrightCart requires full-traffic simultaneous launch across both regions, we should require a short-term reserved capacity commitment (Dedicated) for the first 7 days to avoid disruption to other customers.

Operational items for approval:
1) Canary plan (25% / 6h) — Product approves
2) Fallback model routing rules — Product approves
3) Emergency scale to reserved pool — Product requires Sales to get written commitment from customer

I'll prepare a short playbook (1-pager) for the SRE team with the exact KPIs we want monitored and the rollback thresholds. Assign SRE lead and a pager owner, then we can green-light the temporary quota adjustments.

—Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management — Redwood Inference
